message.content:
**C♯ major** has a key signature of **seven sharps**:

| Sharp | Note |
|-------|------|
| F♯   | F♯   |
| C♯   | C♯   |
| G♯   | G♯   |
| D♯   | D♯   |
| A♯   | A♯   |
| E♯   | E♯   |
| B♯   | B♯   |

(These are the only accidentals that appear in the key signature; all other notes are natural unless otherwise indicated.)

*Note:* C♯ major is enharmonically equivalent to D♭ major, which uses five flats (B♭, E♭, A♭, D♭, G♭). In most contexts, musicians will write the key as D♭ major to avoid the cumbersome seven‑sharp signature.
